在中國常用的幾個 Homebrew mirror，按「少排隊」排序：

| Mirror | 特點 | 排隊風險 |
|---|---|---|
| **阿里雲** `mirrors.aliyun.com` | 商業 CDN，bottles 速度最快也最穩 | 幾乎沒有 |
| **USTC** `mirrors.ustc.edu.cn` | 中科大，學校鏡像中最穩的之一 | 低 |
| **BFSU** `mirrors.bfsu.edu.cn` | 北外，內容同步自 TUNA 但負載較低 | 中低 |
| TUNA（目前） | 清華，官方推薦但流量最大 | **高（你遇到的）** |

**我的建議**：切到**阿里雲**。它是商業基礎設施，不像大學鏡像會出現你看到的 "Waiting in queue... Position: 310"。缺點是 `HOMEBREW_API_DOMAIN` 的路徑格式要注意（阿里雲是 `homebrew-bottles/api`，和 TUNA 結構不完全一樣）。備案可設 USTC。

對應到你這個 repo，要改的是兩個地方（都是 TUNA 寫死）：

- `run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl:74-77`（首次安裝時的環境變數）
- `dot_config/zsh/00_exports.zsh.tmpl:76-79`（日常 shell exports）

阿里雲版本：
```sh
export HOMEBREW_API_DOMAIN="https://mirrors.aliyun.com/homebrew-bottles/api"
export HOMEBREW_BOTTLE_DOMAIN="https://mirrors.aliyun.com/homebrew-bottles"
export HOMEBREW_BREW_GIT_REMOTE="https://mirrors.aliyun.com/homebrew/brew.git"
export HOMEBREW_CORE_GIT_REMOTE="https://mirrors.aliyun.com/homebrew/homebrew-core.git"
```

> ⚠️ 注意 `HOMEBREW_CORE_GIT_REMOTE` 其實在 Homebrew 4.x 之後已經 deprecated（改走 API + JSON），不再做 `git fetch homebrew-core`——所以你現在排隊的 `brew.git` 才是主要痛點，API + bottle domain 換掉影響最大。

要不要我幫你改這兩個檔案，順便在上面加個可切換的註解區塊（`# Alternative: USTC / BFSU ...`）像你 `uv.toml.tmpl` 那樣的風格？

## 關於 fallback 機制

**Homebrew 原生不支援 fallback** — 跟 uv 的 `extra-index-url` 不一樣：

| 生態 | Fallback 支援 | 機制 |
|---|---|---|
| uv / pip | ✅ 有 | `extra-index-url` 陣列，主 index 失敗自動走下一個 |
| Go modules | ✅ 有 | `GOPROXY="url1,url2,direct"` 逗號串接 |
| npm | ⚠️ 半有 | `registry` 單值，但可搭 `.npmrc` scope 分流 |
| cargo | ⚠️ 半有 | `[source.xxx].replace-with` 設定檔切換 |
| **Homebrew** | ❌ **無** | 四個 env var 都只吃單一 URL；掛了就是 `brew install` fail |

所以我才用 comment/uncomment 的方式寫 — 這是「最不 magic、出事最好 debug」的做法。

## 如果真的想做 fallback

三條路，我個人建議 **第 2 個**：

1. **Shell 啟動時 ping 檢測** — 每次開新 shell 都 `curl --head` 四個 mirror 選最快的。→ 會拖慢 zsh 啟動（至少 +200ms），不建議。
2. **加一個 `brew-mirror` 切換函數** — 平常跑 Aliyun，遇到故障時手動 `brew-mirror ustc` 切過去。零啟動開銷，故障時 1 秒切換。
3. **parallel mirror 自動選擇** — 寫個 background health-check daemon 定時更新 `~/.config/homebrew/mirror.env`，shell 啟動 source 它。→ 工程量 >> 收益。

方案 2 可以像這樣放進 `dot_config/zsh/` 某個檔案：

```sh
brew-mirror() {
    case "$1" in
        aliyun) local base="https://mirrors.aliyun.com/homebrew"; local bottles="https://mirrors.aliyun.com/homebrew-bottles" ;;
        ustc)   local base="https://mirrors.ustc.edu.cn";         local bottles="https://mirrors.ustc.edu.cn/homebrew-bottles"; local core_suffix="/homebrew-core.git" ;;
        bfsu)   local base="https://mirrors.bfsu.edu.cn/git/homebrew"; local bottles="https://mirrors.bfsu.edu.cn/homebrew-bottles" ;;
        tuna)   local base="https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/git/homebrew"; local bottles="https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/homebrew-bottles" ;;
        *) echo "usage: brew-mirror {aliyun|ustc|bfsu|tuna}"; return 1 ;;
    esac
    export HOMEBREW_BREW_GIT_REMOTE="${base}/brew.git"
    # ...等
    (cd "$(brew --repo)" && git remote set-url origin "$HOMEBREW_BREW_GIT_REMOTE")
    (cd "$(brew --repo homebrew/core)" 2>/dev/null && git remote set-url origin "$HOMEBREW_CORE_GIT_REMOTE") || true
    echo "Switched to $1"
}
```

注意 USTC 的 `brew.git` 路徑跟其他人不一樣（頂層而不是 `/git/homebrew/`），所以 case 要分開處理，這也是為什麼硬寫 `${base}` 會出錯、我上面只寫雛型。

要不要我幫你把這個函數正式加進去（可能放 `dot_config/zsh/10_functions.zsh` 或類似地方）？如果你用不到快速切換、不想增加表面積，也可以就停在目前 comment block 的版本。

522	### Proxy helpers
523	
524	> Portable loopback-proxy helpers. Honors `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` (+ optional `$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL` for split Clash `socks-port:` configs); otherwise prefers an active Clash config (`mixed-port:` or `port:`/`socks-port:` from `~/.config/clash/config.yaml` or `~/Library/Application Support/clash/config.yaml`) before falling back to probing ports 7890/7891/1087/8118/8080 with `nc -z -w1`. Detection is cached per shell; `proxy-off` and `proxy-refresh` clear that cache before the next lookup. Set `$LOCAL_PROXY_AUTO_ACTIVATE=1` to auto-export env vars on shell startup. Full guide: [docs/tools/web-reader.md](../tools/web-reader.md). See also: [docs/tools/containers.md](../tools/containers.md) for how `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` feeds the chezmoi-managed `~/.docker/config.json` `proxies.default` block.
525	
526	| Command | Type | Source File | Description |
527	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|
528	| `withproxy` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/50_networking.zsh` | Run a single command with proxy env vars exported to the child only (e.g. `withproxy curl ...`) |
529	| `try_direct_then_proxy` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/50_networking.zsh` | Run a command direct; on failure, retry via `withproxy`. Used as the default for reader functions. |
530	| `proxy-on` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/50_networking.zsh` | Export `http_proxy`/`https_proxy`/`HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`/`ALL_PROXY` in the current shell |
531	| `proxy-off` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/50_networking.zsh` | Unset all proxy env vars in the current shell |
532	| `proxy-status` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/50_networking.zsh` | Report state: **active** (exported), **available** (detected), or **unavailable** |
533	| `proxy-refresh` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/50_networking.zsh` | Clear cached detection, re-probe, print status (use after toggling your proxy) |
534

536	
537	> Render web pages as markdown in the terminal. All functions use `try_direct_then_proxy` so non-GFW'd URLs pay zero proxy overhead. Pick the extractor by function name. Full guide: [docs/tools/web-reader.md](../tools/web-reader.md).

584	## AI Capture
585	
586	> One-shot pipeline: capture a past block (via `cpblock N`) and pass it to a coding-agent CLI (claude / opencode / codex / cursor-agent) in non-interactive / advisory mode. Agent auto-detected in the order listed; override with `-a AGENT`. Prompt override via `-p PROMPT`. Agent reply goes to stdout (pipe-friendly: `aifix | tee /tmp/advice.md`), status line to stderr.
587	
588	| Command | Type | Source File | Description |
589	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|

591	| `aiexplain [N] [-a AGENT] [-p PROMPT]` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh` | Capture Nth block (tmux), ask agent to explain what happened |
592	| `aifix-stdin [-a AGENT] [-p PROMPT]` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh` | Non-tmux: read stdin as context, ask agent (`tail -100 log \| aifix-stdin`) |
593	| `aifix-run -- CMD [ARG...]` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh` | Non-tmux: run CMD with stdout+stderr teed, feed to agent |

全部搞定。總結：

**改了 3 個檔案：**
- `run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl` — Homebrew 部分改 Aliyun，其他 3 個 mirror 作為 commented 備案；info log 同步更新
- `dot_config/zsh/00_exports.zsh.tmpl` — 同上，加上「無 fallback 機制」的 note
- `dot_config/zsh/10_aliases.zsh` — 新增 `brew-mirror` 函數（+`docs/zsh/aliases.md` 同步）

**驗證過：**
- 4 個 mirror 端點都 `HTTP 200`（API、bottles、brew.git）
- zsh syntax clean
- `brew-mirror` no-arg / 未知 mirror / 切換 3 種呼叫都行為正確

**上線步驟（你方便時跑）：**
```sh
chezmoi apply              # 推新的 env vars
exec zsh                   # 新 shell 吃到 Aliyun env
brew-mirror aliyun         # 一次性把既有 clone 的 origin 從 TUNA 改寫到 Aliyun
brew update                # 驗證新 remote 通
```

> 第三步是必要的 — 環境變數只控制「未來 brew 要去哪裡 fetch」，但你本機 `$(brew --repo)` 的 `.git/config` 裡的 `origin` 還指向 TUNA。`brew-mirror` 函數的設計就是把這兩件事一起做。

臨時要切換（例如 Aliyun 某天抽風）：`brew-mirror ustc` → 零啟動開銷、1 秒切過去，這就是當初放棄做自動 fallback 換成這個的原因。

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-04-24 18:55:07Z)**_

兩個 root cause 都清楚了：

**Cursor**: `/tmp/cursor.deb` 是 **JSON**，不是 .deb。cursor.com 的 `/api/download` 現在回傳 `{"downloadUrl":"https://downloads.cursor.com/..."}`，不再 302 redirect。要先 GET API、parse JSON，再 download 真正的 URL。

**OpenTofu**: gpgkey 取得沒問題（被 CDN 到 Cloudfront），但要進一步確認 apt repo path 對不對。

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-04-24 18:57:25Z)**_

找到 OpenTofu 的根因了：InRelease 只被 key2 (`packages.opentofu.org/.../gpgkey`) 簽名。key1 (`get.opentofu.org/opentofu.gpg`) 是另一把 **不相關** 的 key — 白寫了。而 `deb-src` 那行在這個 Cloudsmith-style repo 沒有 source 包，也會讓 `apt-get update` 噴錯。

兩個 fix 都動手。先看一下 Cursor 那邊的 task 完整結構：

   bash /tmp/test-opentofu-fix.sh
   ```

   如果噴錯貼回來，我就有真實 stderr 可以再調。如果跑完 `tofu version` 印出版本 → 確認可以 commit。

2. **驗過之後**，3 個 fix 一起 commit：
   - `dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml` — Cursor 改 `uri` → parse `debUrl` → `get_url`
   - `dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml` — Discord 砍掉 `follow: true`（和 Cursor 同個 bug）
   - `dot_ansible/roles/iac_tools/tasks/main.yml` — OpenTofu 單鑰匙 + 砍 `deb-src` + 註解說明為什麼

**3 個改動的要點摘要：**

| 檔案 | 改動 | 原因 |
|---|---|---|
| Cursor task | `get_url` → `uri` (JSON) + `get_url` (debUrl) | `/api/download` 回傳 JSON `{debUrl,rpmUrl,...}`、不再是 binary redirect |
| Discord task | 移除 `follow: true` | 跟 Cursor 同批引入的 bug；`get_url` 默認就會跟 HTTP redirect |
| OpenTofu task | 刪 `get.opentofu.org/opentofu.gpg` + 刪 `deb-src` line | 前者不簽 InRelease（白掛）；後者不需要（我們不裝 source） |

跑完 test script 的結果貼回來，我就幫你 commit。

23	#       ansible-become.yml  0600  `ansible_become_password: "…"` for `-e @`

25	#       chezmoi.pid         0600  ancestor chezmoi PID the watchdog watches
26	#   - Watchdog is detached via `setsid` so a run-script EXIT does not reap it.
27	#     It watches the chezmoi ancestor PID and `rm -rf`s the state dir when
28	#     chezmoi exits. That is the effective end-of-flow cleanup — per-script
29	#     EXIT traps would wipe state before the NEXT run-script could reuse it.
30	#   - INT/TERM/HUP in any consuming script triggers `sudo_session_abort`,
31	#     which kills the watchdog and wipes state immediately.
32	#

35	#                               return. Else probe passwordless sudo; if not

37	#                               write files, spawn watchdog. Returns non-zero if

ansible: fix re-apply idempotency (Cursor force-download, OpenTofu gpg --yes, sudo cache/NOPASSWD distinction)

Three independent re-apply footguns surfaced on the second `chezmoi apply`,
all where ansible tasks mistook cached/prior state for success:

* Cursor: `get_url` defaults to `force: false`, so if /tmp/cursor.deb exists
  from a previous run it silently skips the download (1s elapsed, dead
  giveaway) and `apt install` chokes on the stale JSON with
  "E:Invalid archive signature". Set `force: true` — the URL-based
  download is always cheap vs. the alternative of a stale .deb.
* OpenTofu: `gpg --dearmor -o <file>` refuses to overwrite an existing
  keyring without `--yes`, producing "gpg: dearmoring failed: File exists"
  on every re-apply. Add `--yes`, and `rm -f` the orphan
  opentofu-repo.gpg left over from the old dual-key layout so a stale
  sources.list entry can't wedge `apt update` later.
* sudo_shared.sh: `sudo -n true` succeeds for both NOPASSWD: ALL AND a
  merely cached credential — but sudo credential cache is per-(user, tty)
  under tty_tickets, so ansible's become subprocess (different tty, or
  none) gets "sudo: a password is required" even when the parent shell
  thinks sudo is free. Parse `sudo -n -l` for an explicit NOPASSWD: ALL
  entry instead; fall through to the file-based cached path when the
  user merely has NOPASSWD on specific commands (e.g. xkeysnail) or a
  fresh interactive cache. No doc change needed — the three public
  states (passwordless / cached / non-interactive) are preserved; only
  the detection is corrected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
```

```text
    # Single-key setup: the `InRelease` file is signed by the key at
    # packages.opentofu.org/.../gpgkey (subkey 70DF59811A8B9109). The old
    # dual-key approach also included get.opentofu.org/opentofu.gpg, but that
    # is an unrelated OpenTofu project key that does NOT sign the repo —
    # carrying it in signed-by= bought nothing. `deb-src` is dropped because
    # this Cloudsmith-style repo has no source packages and apt-get update
    # fails on the missing Sources file.
    - name: Install OpenTofu repo and package
      ansible.builtin.shell: |
        set -eo pipefail
        # gpg --dearmor -o <file> refuses to overwrite without --yes; on a
        # re-apply the keyring file exists from the previous run. Use --yes
        # so the task is idempotent.
        curl -fsSL https://packages.opentofu.org/opentofu/tofu/gpgkey \
          | gpg --no-tty --batch --yes --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/opentofu.gpg
        # Clean up the orphan keyring from the old dual-key layout so a
        # stale sources.list entry referencing it cannot wedge apt-get update.
        rm -f /etc/apt/keyrings/opentofu-repo.gpg
        echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/opentofu.gpg] https://packages.opentofu.org/opentofu/tofu/any/ any main" \
          > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/opentofu.list
        apt-get update
```

ansible: retry Cursor .deb download on transient TCP drops (x4, 5s delay)

downloads.cursor.com routes poorly from GFW-region networks and the
174MB fetch frequently dies mid-stream with "Incomplete read,
st.st_size=<partial>". get_url has no native resume, so wrap the task in
ansible's until/retries loop. 4 retries x 5s delay keeps a single bad
session from wedging the whole apply; re-downloading 174MB worst case is
still cheaper than an aborted install.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

## Q2: Cursor 會自動升級嗎？

**會** — 而且比想像中乾淨：

Cursor 的 `dpkg -i` 自己會埋 apt source：
```
/etc/apt/sources.list.d/cursor.sources
  URIs: https://downloads.cursor.com/aptrepo
  Suites: stable  Components: main
  Signed-By: /usr/share/keyrings/anysphere.gpg
apt-cache policy cursor:
  Installed: 3.2.10-1776992904
  Candidate: 3.2.10-1776992904   ← 跟著 upstream 動
```

所以之後 Cursor 發新版，只要跑：
```sh
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade cursor    # 純手動
# 或
just upgrade-system                            # 你 upgrade_tools.sh 的 apt 分類
```

> ⚠️ 注意 CLAUDE.md 的 **install-vs-upgrade split** 鐵則 — `chezmoi apply` **不會**跑 `apt upgrade`。所以 Cursor 自己的 apt source 不會讓 `apply` 自動 bump，這是設計上要的行為。Cursor 本身的 in-app updater 對 .deb 裝法有時能跑（改寫 `/usr/share/cursor/` 需要 sudo，通常會跳 GUI 密碼框），不太可靠。正解是走 `just upgrade-*`。

### ⚠️ Zen 有個 subtle 問題

剛剛 apply log 裡**沒有 `Download Zen AppImage` task**（task 172 後直接跳 173 SVG icon），代表 task 被 `when: zen_appimage_url | length > 0` gate 掉了。也就是說：

1. 我們的 ansible task 期待 Zen 裝在 `~/Applications/zen.AppImage`（固定檔名）
2. `Check if Zen AppImage is already installed` stat 這個路徑 → 不存在（你有的是 `zen-x86_64_fe71...AppImage`）

也就是：**你的 `~/Applications/zen-x86_64_fe71....AppImage` 是目前唯一的 Zen**，刪掉就沒了。

1:# AppImage & AppImageLauncher on Ubuntu
5:The gap is desktop integration: a bare `~/Applications/foo.AppImage` doesn't show up in the GNOME/KDE launcher, has no `.desktop` entry, and doesn't get picked up by `xdg-open`. That's where **[AppImageLauncher](https://github.com/TheAssassin/AppImageLauncher)** comes in — a system daemon that watches a directory for AppImages and auto-integrates them (icon extraction, `.desktop` generation, optional move into a canonical location, optional update-via-delta).
7:This repo installs AppImageLauncher on `ubuntu_desktop` machines via the [`gui_apps_linux`](../../dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml) Ansible role. This doc covers the *why*, the three install paths, and the two footguns you'll hit on current Ubuntu.
9:## Why AppImageLauncher vs bare AppImages vs `appimaged`
15:| **AppImageLauncher** (this repo) | Yes | Yes (opt-in) | Yes (Lite) | First-run modal asks "Integrate or Run once?", stores integrated AppImages in `~/Applications/`, handles removal cleanly. |
17:The **first-run prompt** is the real win: double-click an AppImage and AppImageLauncher asks whether to install it system-wide (move to `~/Applications/`, generate `.desktop` + icon + MIME handlers) or run once and delete. Makes AppImages feel like regular apps without locking you into yet another store.
19:## Install paths
23:### 1. Ubuntu PPA (preferred on 20.04 / 22.04 LTS)
33:### 2. GitHub `.deb` fallback (needed on 24.04 "noble")
35:The PPA [has no release for Ubuntu 24.04](https://github.com/TheAssassin/AppImageLauncher/issues) as of 2026; maintainership has stalled. The latest `.deb` from the GitHub releases page still installs cleanly on noble:
39:curl -fsSL "https://api.github.com/repos/TheAssassin/AppImageLauncher/releases/latest" \
47:### 3. AppImageLauncher **Lite** (no root, user-level)
49:Lite is AppImageLauncher shipped as an AppImage itself — integrates itself into `~/.config/autostart`, `~/.local/share/applications`, `~/.local/share/icons`. Useful on locked-down machines where you can't `sudo`.
52:mkdir -p ~/Applications
53:curl -fsSL "https://api.github.com/repos/TheAssassin/AppImageLauncher/releases/latest" \
55:  | xargs -I{} curl -fSL -o ~/Applications/appimagelauncher-lite.AppImage {}
56:chmod +x ~/Applications/appimagelauncher-lite.AppImage
57:~/Applications/appimagelauncher-lite.AppImage install   # one-time integration
62:## `ail-cli` — scripted integration
64:The system daemon provides `ail-cli` for headless integration. Useful for provisioning scripts that drop AppImages into `~/Applications/` and want them to appear in the launcher without a double-click.

回答你真正的問題 —

## 為什麼 Cursor 在 `/usr/share/`、Zen 在 `~/Applications/`？

**短答：用 upstream 給的最 robust 的包裝格式。**

| Upstream 給什麼 | 選哪個 | 裝到哪 | 升級路徑 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 官方 `.deb` | `.deb` | `/usr/share/<app>/` + `/usr/bin/<app>` | `dpkg` 會自己埋 apt source → `apt upgrade` 走得通 |
| 只有 AppImage | AppImage | `~/Applications/<app>.AppImage` | 重新下載（AppImageLauncher 可以 delta update）|
| 只有 tarball / 源碼 | case-by-case | `~/Applications/<app>/` 或 `/opt/<app>/` | 手動 |

Cursor 有 `.deb` → 用 `.deb` → 自動拿到 `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/cursor.sources` → `apt upgrade` 自動對接 → **這是最爽的路徑**。
Zen 官方 release 沒 `.deb` → 只能 AppImage → 放 `~/Applications/zen.AppImage`（固定檔名，不帶 hash）→ 靠 AppImageLauncher 做 desktop 整合。

## 為什麼 `.deb` 能順帶裝 apt source（你的第二個問題）

這不是 dpkg/apt 的魔法，是 **`.deb` 的 postinst script 做的**。現代商業軟體的 `.deb`（Cursor、Chrome、VSCode、Signal、Discord）包裡都有 `DEBIAN/postinst`，在 `dpkg -i` 之後會：

1. 寫一個 `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/<app>.sources`（或 `.list`）
2. 把它們的 signing key 放到 `/usr/share/keyrings/<app>.gpg`
3. 之後 `apt update` 會從那個 repo 拉 `Packages` 清單，正常 upgrade 機制接管

你可以 `dpkg -I cursor_3.2.10_amd64.deb` 看那個 package 的 metadata，裡面會有 postinst。`dpkg -L cursor | grep sources` 也能確認檔案是 .deb 帶的還是 apt 產生的。

這邊沒有違反你 `CLAUDE.md` 的 **install-vs-upgrade split** — `chezmoi apply` 本身不跑 `apt upgrade`，Cursor 能吃到更新是因為使用者「有一天」跑了 `apt upgrade` 或 `just upgrade-system`。

## 建議的 SOP：unified GUI-app packaging

`docs/tools/appimage.md` 已經講了 AppImageLauncher；缺的是**選哪個包裝 + 為什麼**的決策樹。寫個新 doc `docs/tools/linux-gui-apps.md`（或擴 appimage.md），內容包括：

1. **決策樹**（上面那張表）
2. **.deb auto-repo mechanism**（postinst 原理）
3. **AppImage 規範**：
   - 一律放 `~/Applications/<app>.AppImage`（fixed filename，不帶 version/hash）
   - 一律走 AppImageLauncher + 手寫 `.desktop` 那套流程
   - Re-apply 會覆蓋（ansible task 的 `when: not stat.exists` 意味著**不自動升版**；要升級走 `just upgrade-*`）
4. **User workflow**：
   - 想裝新 GUI app：先看 upstream 有沒有 `.deb`；有就走 `apt install <foo.deb>`，沒有就手動丟 `~/Applications/`
   - 要把自己手動裝的 AppImage 交給 AppImageLauncher 管：雙擊 .AppImage → 選 Integrate
   - 要查 GUI app 怎麼升級：`apt show <pkg>` 看有沒有 apt source；沒有就是 AppImage，重下或 `just upgrade-*`
5. **Dotfiles maintainer workflow**（新增 GUI app 到 ansible role 時的 checklist）

**對應要碰的檔案：**
- `docs/tools/linux-gui-apps.md`（新，或 append 到 `appimage.md`）
- `mkdocs.yml` nav 加一行（如果開新檔案）
- `CLAUDE.md` 的 "Cross-file maintenance rules" 加一小段 invariant：「新增 GUI app 到 `gui_apps_linux` 時，先看 upstream 提供 `.deb` 還是 AppImage，按決策樹選 task pattern」
- 順手把 `dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml` 頂部的 header comment 寫個 summary 指向這個 doc

要不要我按這個骨架寫出 doc + 加 CLAUDE.md 的 invariant？我建議分兩個 commit：
1. `docs: linux-gui-apps SOP + decision tree (.deb auto-repo vs AppImage)`
2. `ansible: top-of-file header pointing to the SOP`

寫完後再單獨查 Zen task skip 的事（可能要加 `debug:` 把 `zen_appimage_url` 印出來 repro 一次才知道原因）。

```text
# repos: Alacritty (cargo), AppImageLauncher (PPA / .deb / Lite), VSCode
# (Microsoft apt repo), Cursor (.deb with graceful fallback), Discord (.deb,
# x86_64-only), Zen Browser (AppImage + .desktop), libfuse2 (AppImage runtime
# on Ubuntu 22.04+), and a placeholder hook for Antigravity once an official
# Linux package ships.
#
# No-op on:
#   - macOS  → Brewfile (`cask "alacritty"`, `cask "visual-studio-code"` when
#              you add them) covers the desktop story. This role emits a
#              debug note only on Darwin, no install logic runs.
#   - armhf  → 32-bit ARM has no practical GUI story; cargo builds are slow
#              and AppImages lack first-class armv7 support.
#   - noRoot → `--skip-tags sudo` (set by run_onchange) skips every system
#              apt/deb/PPA task. AppImageLauncher Lite (user-level AppImage)
#              still runs when `gui_apps_linux_no_root=true` is passed via
#              `--extra-vars`.
#
# Editor user-config overlays (settings.json / keybindings.json) are handled
# by chezmoi itself, NOT ansible — see `.chezmoitemplates/editor/` and the
# `modify_settings.json.tmpl` / `create_keybindings.json.tmpl` source files.
# =============================================================================

# --- Platform banner ---

- name: Announce gui_apps_linux is Linux-only (macOS uses Brewfile)
  when: ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Darwin'
  ansible.builtin.debug:
    msg: >-
      gui_apps_linux is Linux-only. macOS GUI apps are declared in
      dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl (alacritty cask, etc.).

- name: Skip gui_apps_linux on armhf
  when:
    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
    - target_architecture == 'armv7l'
  ansible.builtin.debug:
    msg: >-
      Skipping gui_apps_linux on armhf — no practical GUI stack,
      cargo builds of alacritty are very slow, and upstream AppImages
--
# AppImageLauncher — desktop integration for AppImages
#
# Strategy (in order):
#   1. PPA `ppa:appimagelauncher-team/stable` — preferred on 20.04/22.04.
#   2. GitHub `.deb` fallback — PPA is known-broken on Ubuntu 24.04 "noble"
#      as of 2026 (upstream has not published a noble release); the latest
#      GitHub `.deb` still installs cleanly.
#   3. AppImageLauncher **Lite** — a user-level AppImage that integrates
#      itself without root. Enabled when `gui_apps_linux_no_root=true`.
#
# Docs: see docs/tools/appimage.md for install paths, ail-cli usage, and
# the libfuse2 / AppArmor gotchas on recent Ubuntu.
# =============================================================================

- name: Check if AppImageLauncher is installed (system-wide)
  when:
    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
    - target_architecture != 'armv7l'
  ansible.builtin.command: dpkg -s appimagelauncher
  register: ail_check
```

 workflow.md
---workflow playbook sample structure---
# Development Workflow — "Only type where you're going"

The end-to-end flow for picking up a project, jumping between worktrees, and
running parallel AI coding agents — without memorising helper function names.

This doc is the **index**. For deep dives see
[`docs/tools/sesh.md`](../tools/sesh.md) (picker, layouts, sesh config),
[`docs/tools/worktrunk.md`](../tools/worktrunk.md) (worktrees, parallel agents,
hooks), and [`docs/tools/tmux/`](../tools/tmux/) (panes, popup menu, theme).

---

## TL;DR — one key per intent

| Intent | Key | Where the key lives |
|---|---|---|
| Switch project / open a new one | `Alt+S` (outside tmux) or `prefix+g` (inside) | `smart-picker.sh` |
| Switch branch within current project | inside the picker → `Ctrl+W` worktrees | `smart-picker.sh` |
| Spin up a new parallel branch + agent | `wt cc <branch> -- '<prompt>'` | [`worktrunk.md`](../tools/worktrunk.md#per-worktree-claude--opencode) |
| Peek at sibling worktree (no session swap) | `wtcd` (fzf-tmux picker) | [`worktrunk.md`](../tools/worktrunk.md#the-wtcd-rationale) |
| Refresh coding-agent layout on current repo | `scode` (manual override) | [`sesh.md`](../tools/sesh.md) |

Everything else is explained by these five rows.

---

## The one keystroke

- **Outside tmux** (plain zsh prompt): `Alt+S`
- **Inside tmux**: `prefix + g`

Both open the same fzf popup. Same hotkeys, same behaviour, same dispatch
logic. The only difference is that outside-tmux spawns a fresh tmux client,
inside-tmux uses `switch-client` — handled by `sesh connect` and
`_sesh_attach_or_switch` transparently.

### Filter modes inside the picker

```
 ^a all         sesh list --icons
```

```md
# Linux GUI Apps — packaging mechanisms, this repo's strategy, and how to add a new one

Ubuntu has **five** packaging mechanisms for desktop apps. They differ in
*where binaries land*, *whether anything keeps them current*, and *how
desktop integration (icon, `.desktop`, MIME handlers) gets wired up*.

This doc:

1. lays out the five mechanisms and the trade-off matrix,
2. inventories every GUI app this repo's `gui_apps_linux` ansible role
   knows about (plus the snaps you probably installed via Ubuntu App
   Center), so you can tell at a glance which path each app is on,
3. gives a decision tree for adding a *new* app to the role.

## TL;DR — five mechanisms, one trade-off matrix

| Mechanism | Auto-update? | Install scope | Desktop integration | Sandbox |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`.deb` w/ apt-source postinst** | ✅ via `apt upgrade` | system-wide (`/usr/share/...`) | ✅ baked in | ❌ |
| **`.deb` w/o apt-source postinst** | ❌ manual re-deploy | system-wide | ✅ baked in | ❌ |
| **Snap** (Ubuntu App Center) | ✅ `snapd` background daemon | `/snap/<app>/<rev>/` | ✅ baked in | ✅ confined |
| **Flatpak** (Flathub) | ✅ `flatpak update` | per-user `~/.var/app/...` | ✅ baked in | ✅ confined |
| **AppImage + AppImageLauncher** | ❌ re-download | per-user `~/Applications/` | ✅ via AIL daemon | ❌ |
| Cargo / from source | ❌ via `cargo install --force` | per-user `~/.cargo/bin/` | ❌ manual `.desktop` | ❌ |
| Tarball / `.tar.xz` | ❌ pure manual | per-user (anywhere) | ❌ manual | ❌ |

The **green-checkmark `.deb` row is the gold standard** when upstream
provides it. Snap and Flatpak are the auto-update fallbacks for vendors
who don't ship `.deb` (or who want sandboxing). AppImage is the
last-mile bridge for everyone else.

## Inventory of GUI apps on this machine

### Ansible-managed (this repo)

| App | Mechanism | Auto-update? | Source-of-truth | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Cursor** | `.deb` (auto-adds `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/cursor.sources`) | ✅ `apt upgrade cursor` | [`gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml) "Install Cursor via .deb" | `/usr/share/cursor/` |
| **VSCode** | `.deb` (auto-adds `vscode.sources`) | ✅ `apt upgrade code` | same role | `/usr/share/code/` |
| **Discord** | `.deb` (no apt source — see "Discord auto-update" below) | ❌ | same role | `/usr/share/discord/` |
| **Zen Browser** | AppImage at `~/Applications/zen.AppImage` (stable filename, no version suffix) | ❌ — re-run ansible task | same role | `~/Applications/zen.AppImage` |
| **Alacritty** | `cargo install alacritty` | ❌ — `just upgrade-cargo` | [`devtools` role](../../dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml) | `~/.cargo/bin/alacritty` |
| **AppImageLauncher** | `.deb` (PPA on 22.04, GitHub release on 24.04) | ✅ via apt | same role | system + `appimagelauncherd.service` (user) |
| **Bitwarden CLI** (`bw`) | npm via mise (separate from desktop app) | ❌ — `just upgrade-mise` | mise | `~/.local/share/mise/...` |

### Manually managed (you installed these yourself, outside ansible)

| App | Mechanism | Auto-update? | How it got there | How to upgrade |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Bitwarden Desktop** | Snap (publisher `bitwarden`) | ✅ background | `snap install bitwarden` (or App Center) | `snap refresh bitwarden` |
| **Spotify** | Snap (publisher `Spotify**`) | ✅ background | Ubuntu App Center | `snap refresh spotify` |
| **Firefox** | Snap (canonical default since Ubuntu 22.04) | ✅ background | preinstalled with the OS | `snap refresh firefox` |
| **btop** | Snap (kz6fittycent) | ✅ background | manual | `snap refresh btop` |
| **Frpc Desktop** | AppImage at `~/Applications/Frpc-Desktop-1.2.1.AppImage` | ❌ — manual re-download | manual drop-in | overwrite the file |
| **Clash for Windows** | tarball at `~/Documents/ClashForWindows/` ⚠️ | ❌ **DEPRECATED upstream** | extracted manually 2025 | **Migrate** — see below |

> **Clash for Windows is dead.** The original developer (Fndroid)
> publicly stopped maintenance in **2023-11** and the GitHub repo is
> archived. No new releases, no CVE patches. Migrate to one of the
> maintained forks:
>
> - [Clash Verge Rev](https://github.com/clash-verge-rev/clash-verge-rev) — active fork, ships .deb + AppImage
> - [Clash Nyanpasu](https://github.com/libnyanpasu/clash-nyanpasu) — Tauri-based GUI, AppImage + .deb
> - [Mihomo Party](https://github.com/mihomo-party-org/mihomo-party) — successor of CFW UX, AppImage + .deb
>
> All three publish `.deb` packages — drop the new app into `gui_apps_linux`
> following the [Cursor `.deb` pattern](#deb-pattern) and delete
> `~/Documents/ClashForWindows/` after the new one is wired up.

## Why `.deb` auto-update works (the apt-source postinst trick)

When `dpkg -i cursor_<v>_amd64.deb` runs, Cursor's package contains a
`DEBIAN/postinst` script that, on success, writes:

- `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/cursor.sources` — pointing at `https://downloads.cursor.com/aptrepo`
- `/usr/share/keyrings/anysphere.gpg` — the signing key

After that, `apt update` pulls Cursor's release index alongside Ubuntu's
own, and `apt upgrade cursor` (or generic `apt upgrade` / `just upgrade-system`)
treats it like any other apt package. The user never needs to revisit
cursor.com.

You can verify this for any installed `.deb`:

\```sh
dpkg -L cursor | grep -E 'sources|keyring'
# /etc/apt/sources.list.d/cursor.sources
# /usr/share/keyrings/anysphere.gpg
\```

VSCode, Chrome, Signal, 1Password, Slack, Microsoft Edge, Brave all
follow this pattern. **Discord does not** — see the next section.

## Discord auto-update — why the screenshot keeps appearing

Discord's `.deb` does **not** ship a postinst that adds an apt source:

\```sh
dpkg -L discord | grep -E 'sources|keyring'
# (empty)
\```

So `apt upgrade` is never aware of new Discord releases. Discord's
in-app updater detects the version mismatch, but on Linux it can't
actually invoke `dpkg` (no root) — so it pops the *"Must be your lucky
day, there's a new update!"* modal with a "Download" button that just
opens the vendor download page. You then have to manually `dpkg -i` the
new `.deb`.

Three ways out:

1. **Re-run the ansible task on demand**: `chezmoi apply` (the role
   re-fetches the latest `.deb` URL via Discord's API every apply).
   This is what we do for Cursor too, so it's consistent.
2. **Switch to Flatpak**: `flatpak install flathub com.discordapp.Discord`.
   Flatpak auto-updates via `flatpak update`. Loses some native
   integration (notifications via XDG portal, screen-share via
   PipeWire) but the upgrade story is clean.
3. **Switch to Vesktop / WebCord** (community Discord clients with
   self-update). Drift from official Discord; not recommended unless
   you're already running modded Discord.

For **Discord pain specifically** the cheapest fix is option 1 — add a
`just upgrade-discord` recipe (or fold it into `just upgrade-system`)
that re-runs the ansible task. The ansible task already does the
"latest version via API" resolution, so it's idempotent: nothing
happens if you're already on the current release.

## Snap (Ubuntu App Center) — what's actually happening

The Ubuntu App Center is a GTK frontend for `snapd` — Canonical's
universal package manager that ships `.snap` archives from the Snap
Store. When you install **Bitwarden** or **Spotify** from App Center:

- The `.snap` file is extracted to `/snap/<app>/<rev>/` (versioned,
  read-only)
- A symlink `/snap/<app>/current` always points at the active rev
- A wrapper script at `/snap/bin/<app>` is what `$PATH` actually picks up
- A user-systemd service `snapd.refresh.service` checks for updates
  ~4× per day and applies them in the background
- Desktop integration (`/var/lib/snapd/desktop/applications/<app>.desktop`)
  is auto-generated; the snap-store daemon updates these on refresh

This means **Bitwarden Desktop and Spotify will keep themselves up to
date with no manual action** — the same way `apt upgrade` doesn't run
automatically but apt-source `.deb`s are kept current via your existing
`just upgrade-system` cadence, snaps are kept current via `snapd`'s
*always-on* refresh daemon. Different paradigm, same end result.

To inspect: `snap list`, `snap info <app>`, `snap refresh --list`
(pending updates), `snap refresh <app>` (force-refresh now), `snap
revert <app>` (rollback to previous rev — neat property of the
versioned `/snap/<app>/<rev>/` layout).

> Caveat: snaps run in a confinement sandbox, which can break power-user
> workflows (no access to `~/.ssh` by default for example). Most desktop
> apps work fine; CLI tools sometimes don't. Prefer `.deb` or apt
> when both options exist.

## AppImage + AppImageLauncher — the catch-all

When upstream ships only an AppImage (Zen Browser, Cursor's old AppImage,
many indie tools), our convention is:

1. **Stable filename**: drop the file at `~/Applications/<app>.AppImage`
   (no version or hash in the name). Re-runs of the ansible task just
   overwrite it. Files like `zen-x86_64_fe71259e...AppImage` (old hash
   suffix in filename) are the wrong shape — they accumulate forever.
2. **Executable bit**: `mode: '0755'` in the ansible task.
3. **AppImageLauncher integration**: `appimagelauncherd.service` (user
   systemd unit, set up by our role) watches `~/Applications/`. New
   AppImages trigger a first-run modal: *"Integrate or Run once?"* —
   integrating extracts the icon, generates a `.desktop` entry under
   `~/.local/share/applications/`, and (optionally) moves the file to
   AppImageLauncher's canonical location.

For our managed AppImages we usually skip the modal by writing the
`.desktop` entry ourselves in the same ansible task — see Zen Browser.
For AppImages you drop manually (Frpc Desktop), let the modal handle it.

To check the daemon: `systemctl --user status appimagelauncherd`.
Manual integration: `ail-cli integrate ~/Applications/foo.AppImage`.

## Adding a new GUI app to `gui_apps_linux`

\```
Does upstream publish a .deb?
├─ YES → Does the .deb add an apt source (check `dpkg -L <pkg> | grep sources` after install)?
│        ├─ YES → use the .deb. Ansible installs once, apt keeps current. ★ best path
│        └─ NO  → use the .deb anyway, BUT add a refresh hook to
│                 `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh` so `just upgrade-system`
│                 re-fetches latest. (Discord pattern.)
│
├─ NO ── Does upstream publish on Snap or Flatpak with FIRST-PARTY support?
│        ├─ Official Snap → use snap (community.general.snap module).
│        │                 Cleanest auto-update on Ubuntu, but confined.
│        ├─ Official Flathub → use flatpak (community.general.flatpak module).
│        │                    Cross-distro friendly, also confined.
│        └─ Community-only → skip; AppImage probably more reliable.
│
└─ Only AppImage / tarball?
   ├─ AppImage → drop in ~/Applications/ as <app>.AppImage. AIL integrates.
   └─ tarball  → ~/Applications/<app>/ + wrapper script + manual .desktop.
                 ⚠️ Last resort — no auto-update path, manual everything.
\```

### Concrete patterns

**`.deb` pattern** — see "Install Cursor via .deb" in
[`gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml).
Two-step:

1. `ansible.builtin.uri` — fetch vendor's API to resolve the latest
   `.deb` URL (return JSON, parse `debUrl` or similar field).
2. `ansible.builtin.get_url` — download the `.deb`, with `force: true`
   (overwrite stale files from prior apply) and `until: cursor_dl is
   succeeded` + `retries: 4` + `delay: 5` (GFW-region CDN drops).
3. `ansible.builtin.apt: deb=<path>` — install. Postinst handles apt
   source if vendor ships one.
4. Wrap the whole block in `rescue:` that prints a manual-fallback URL.

**AppImage pattern** — see "Install Zen Browser AppImage" in the same
file. Three-step:

1. `ansible.builtin.uri` — GitHub releases API (or vendor equivalent)
   to resolve the asset URL.
2. `selectattr('name', 'match', '^<prefix>-<arch>\\.AppImage$')` filter
   to pick the right asset for `target_architecture` (already normalized
   to `x86_64` / `aarch64` by the `Set target_architecture from dpkg` task
   in [`linux.yml`](../../dot_ansible/playbooks/linux.yml)).
3. `ansible.builtin.get_url` to `~/Applications/<app>.AppImage` with
   `mode: '0755'` and a stable filename.
4. Write a `.desktop` entry under `~/.local/share/applications/` using
   `ansible.builtin.copy` with a `content:` literal — the file gets
   merged into the system menu via `update-desktop-database`.

**Snap pattern** — none yet in this repo. Template:

\```yaml
- name: Install Bitwarden Desktop via Snap
  community.general.snap:
    name: bitwarden
    state: present
    classic: false   # most apps are confined; set true only when vendor docs say so
  become: true
\```

**Flatpak pattern** — none yet. Template:

\```yaml
- name: Install Discord via Flatpak (instead of .deb)
  community.general.flatpak:
    name: com.discordapp.Discord
    state: present
    remote: flathub  # add `community.general.flatpak_remote` first if missing
    method: user     # per-user install; `system` requires root
\```

Always add a `rescue:` block that points the user at the manual
fallback URL (cursor.com / discord.com / GitHub release page) so a
failed automated install isn't a dead end.

```text
1	# AppImage & AppImageLauncher on Ubuntu
2	
3	[AppImage](https://appimage.org/) is a single-file app format for Linux: download, `chmod +x`, run. No root, no install step, no dependencies beyond the host's `libc` and `libfuse2`. The format is how Cursor, Obsidian, Joplin, Bitwarden Desktop, and many AI / markdown / media tools ship their Linux builds.
4	
5	The gap is desktop integration: a bare `~/Applications/foo.AppImage` doesn't show up in the GNOME/KDE launcher, has no `.desktop` entry, and doesn't get picked up by `xdg-open`. That's where **[AppImageLauncher](https://github.com/TheAssassin/AppImageLauncher)** comes in — a system daemon that watches a directory for AppImages and auto-integrates them (icon extraction, `.desktop` generation, optional move into a canonical location, optional update-via-delta).
6	
7	This repo installs AppImageLauncher on `ubuntu_desktop` machines via the [`gui_apps_linux`](../../dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml) Ansible role. This doc covers the *why*, the three install paths, and the two footguns you'll hit on current Ubuntu.
8	
9	## Why AppImageLauncher vs bare AppImages vs `appimaged`
10	
11	| Approach | Desktop menu? | Auto-updates? | No root? | Notes |
12	|---|---|---|---|---|
13	| Bare `chmod +x ./foo.AppImage` | No | No | Yes | Fine for one-offs; nothing shows in launcher. |
14	| [`appimaged`](https://github.com/probonopd/go-appimage) daemon | Yes | Yes (via zsync) | Yes | Watches dirs and writes `.desktop` entries. Less actively maintained; no first-run prompt. |
15	| **AppImageLauncher** (this repo) | Yes | Yes (opt-in) | Yes (Lite) | First-run modal asks "Integrate or Run once?", stores integrated AppImages in `~/Applications/`, handles removal cleanly. |
16	
17	The **first-run prompt** is the real win: double-click an AppImage and AppImageLauncher asks whether to install it system-wide (move to `~/Applications/`, generate `.desktop` + icon + MIME handlers) or run once and delete. Makes AppImages feel like regular apps without locking you into yet another store.
18	
19	## Install paths
20
